text:
Maria H: FYI — dumped the telemetry from last night's staging perf run. Notable: SM occupancy spikes on >1024 seq, VRAM climbs steadily over long sessions, and one host reported thermal_throttle events around 03:12 UTC. Posting links/queries below.

Ajay P: Can you attach the per-route token-level latency breakdown? especially chat vs embeddings.

Maria H: sure — high-level PromQL I used:
```
# 95th SM occupancy by GPU (5m window)
avg by (gpu) (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(sm_occupancy_bucket[5m])) by (le,gpu)))

# token-level latency breakdown (p50,p95,p99) per route
quantile_over_time(0.5, token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]) by (route), quantile_over_time(0.95, token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]) by (route)
```
Link to the dashboard snapshot: https://dashboards.internal/r/telemetry/1759501234 (staging cluster).

Ken L: I pulled a quick kv-cache sample and correlated misses with tail latency. Small excerpt:
```
kv_event,route=chat.completion seq=512 hit=false latency_ms=158 host=gpu-07
kv_event,route=chat.completion seq=64 hit=true latency_ms=24 host=gpu-07
kv_event,route=embeddings seq=128 hit=true latency_ms=18 host=gpu-09
```
The misses are mostly on long seqs and when MIG slices change (we had a slice resize on gpu-07 at 02:55).

perf-bot: Profiling trace uploaded: https://storage.internal/prof/trace-1759501234.flame.html — shows long kernel selection times inside our selector when sequence > 1024. Flame shows ~35% time in kernel_selector.edge_case_branch.

Ajay P: Is the selector doing extra checks when VRAM > 24GB? That could be adding branching. Also, any thermal throttling would reduce clock and change kernel perf counters.

Maria H: good call. The selector has a safety path that triggers when estimated vram_used + kv_cache_est > 0.95 * vram_total. That safety path prefers conservative kernels but currently re-evaluates per-batch which is expensive.

Ken L: Repro script I used on staging (snip):
```bash
# generate long seq requests to reproduce tail
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
    -d '{"route":"chat.completion","seq_len":1024,"prompt":"x"}' 
    https://staging.api.internal/v1/generate &
done
```
This reproduces the SM occupancy spike and the kv-cache miss pattern tied to prefetchtimer expiry.

deploy-bot: Canary revert applied: deploy-2026-03-07T02:50 -> rolled back to deploy-2026-03-06T21:10 (reason: perf regression detected).

Maria H: OK next steps I propose:
- Short term: disable per-batch re-eval of the safety path; instead compute once per-batch-window (5s) and cache.
- Mid term: add a lightweight fast-path kernel selection for seq >= 1024 that avoids branching based on VRAM estimate.
- Observability: add a token-level metric that tags `kv_cache_hit` and `selector_path` so we can correlate hits/misses and which selector branch was used.
- Ops: add thermal alert that correlates host throttling to percent increase in p95 token latency.

Ajay P: +1. I can add the metric tagging this morning and wire it to per-route KPIs.

Ken L: I'll put together a microbenchmark for the selector fast-path and test on MIG slices (1g/2g/4g) to ensure stability.

Maria H: Thanks — I'll open a short-lived RFC for the selector change and tag you both. If anyone else wants to review the flamegraph or kv samples they're at the links above. :thumbsup:
